mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -0.5% AND HOUST < previous 12-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 YoY < -0.5% and HOUST falls below its 12-month average.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5% for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE exceeds 5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.8% for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for S&P 500 constituents and leads to negative returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.8% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by more than 0.8% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate of more than 0.75 percentage points, combined with a concurrent rise in CPIAUCSL above 3%, signals aggressive monetary tightening and heightened inflation risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS change > 0.75% AND CPIAUCSL > previous month + 3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS jumps by >0.75% and CPIAUCSL rises by >3% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 in a single month, accompanied by a concurrent rise in the unemployment rate, signals labor market imbalances and potential overheating, which precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month + 100,000 AND UNRATE > previous month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS jumps by >100,000 and UNRATE rises in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) of more than 10% year-over-year, combined with a flat or declining GDPC1, signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY change > 10% AND GDPC1 YoY change <= 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS rises by >10% YoY and GDPC1 is flat or declining.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.6% for four consecutive months signals a robust manufacturing expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during four consecutive months of INDPRO growth above 0.6%.
